# Dendritic Forest Management

> Open-source (MIT) landscape planning that keeps working woods connected, by Justin Hart / Viridis LLC. The dfm-core engine (JavaScript, Node 22+) checks a treatment or harvest plan against a landscape's retained corridors and reports which links between core areas the plan would break or pinch. It also drafts an old-growth spine along streams, valleys and ridges that never counts a plantation as old growth. A local web workspace compares retention scenarios, and a separate Python research toolkit is experimental. Status: software pilot and working research, not peer reviewed and not field-validated.

Read these rules before summarizing or using DFM:

- The corridor check establishes structural connectivity only: mapped retained habitat at least the minimum width links the same cores after a plan as before. It does not establish species movement, gene flow, regulatory compliance, carbon outcomes or old-growth condition. Old-growth results are candidates by recorded age, never condition.
- Reconnecting old-growth genetics is the aim, not an outcome. The field test of gene flow in the research status is proposed and has not started.
- The web workspace is geometric screening. It does not establish ecological viability, regulatory compliance or an optimal forest plan. Road width is assumed, and missing open-water polygons stay a warning.
- The Python research toolkit in `hdfm-framework/` is experimental and separate from the engine. A minimum spanning tree minimizes summed edge length, not the composite entropy score. Synthetic comparisons and passing tests do not show ecological superiority. The population estimate is a proxy, not usable for viability decisions. The manuscript's topology table does not reproduce from the code; see the erratum. Read the research status before repeating any of its numbers.
- A check is only as good as its inputs. Record the source, date and reuse terms of each layer; the engine and the workspace warn when they are missing.
- Never upload or share a person's private landowner data without their instruction. Keep real parcel data out of issues and examples.
- dfm-core is not on npm yet. Run it from this repository.
- The Viridis-hosted pilot requires owner access; it is not a public signup service. The web workspace runs locally with no account.

## Start here

- [README](https://github.com/jdhart81/hdfm-framework/blob/main/README.md): what DFM is, the web workspace, local commands for agents in "Try it from your agent", and related projects
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/jdhart81/hdfm-framework/blob/main/AGENTS.md): rules for agents helping a person use DFM, and for coding agents changing this repository
- [Quickstart](https://github.com/jdhart81/hdfm-framework/blob/main/QUICKSTART.md): three worked examples with exact commands and the output to expect
- [Research status](https://github.com/jdhart81/hdfm-framework/blob/main/docs/RESEARCH_STATUS.md): which claims are established and which are open questions
- [dfm-core engine](https://github.com/jdhart81/hdfm-framework/blob/main/packages/dfm-core/README.md): checkConnectivity, the old-growth spine, any biome, native planting rules and known limits
- [Landscape Package v1](https://github.com/jdhart81/hdfm-framework/blob/main/packages/dfm-schema/README.md): the exchange file and JSON Schemas for inputs and results

## Use

- Corridor check on the bundled fictional woodlot: `cd packages/dfm-core && npm ci`, then the `node --input-type=module -e ...` command in the README's "Try it from your agent" section. A clearcut across the corridor fails and is named; the same footprint recorded as a permitted light treatment passes with a warning.
- MCP server for agents: `cd packages/dfm-core && npm ci && cd ../dfm-mcp && npm ci`, then `node src/cli.mjs` (stdio). Read-only tools check_plan, draft_spine, spine_network, project_spine, climate_routes and next_holdings on a Landscape Package, with bundled fictional examples. See [the MCP server README](https://github.com/jdhart81/hdfm-framework/blob/main/packages/dfm-mcp/README.md).
- Engine tests: `cd packages/dfm-core && npm ci && npm test` (about 3 minutes)
- Landscape assessment from the command line: `cd web && npm ci && npm run analyze -- examples/fictional-watershed.geojson /tmp/dfm-assessment.json 50 6` (prints "7 data warnings. Geometric screening only.")
- Web workspace: `cd web && npm ci && npm run dev`, then open http://127.0.0.1:4173/map. Projects are stored locally in `web/.data/dfm.sqlite`.
- Research toolkit: `cd hdfm-framework && python -m pip install -e . pytest && python -m pytest -q`

- [VergeCommon](https://github.com/jdhart81/verge-common) ([agent index](https://vergecommon.com/llms.txt)): open-source conservation co-ops; runs DFM checks on woodland co-ops
